root_cause: The exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox includes both data-checkbox-exclusive and data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms", while the working contact group's exclusive checkbox only has data-checkbox-exclusive. This extra attribute may prevent the initialization script from recognizing it as the exclusive option for the symptoms group.
repair_strategy: Remove the data-checkbox-exclusive-group attribute from the exclusive 'No symptoms' checkbox so only the non-exclusive symptom checkboxes carry the group identifier, matching the working contact pattern where the exclusive checkbox has only data-checkbox-exclusive.

edits.before: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive data-checkbox-exclusive-group="symptoms">
edits.after: <input class="nhsuk-checkboxes__input" id="symptoms-none" name="symptoms[none]" type="checkbox" value="yes" data-checkbox-exclusive>

expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard and mouse users can now select the exclusive 'No symptoms' option and have any previously selected symptom choices automatically cleared, providing correct exclusive choice behavior and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 keyboard operability and 4.1.2 name, role, value requirements.
functional_risks: If the script relies on the exclusive checkbox having the group attribute to identify the group, this could break exclusive behavior.
The non-exclusive symptom checkboxes retain the group attribute, which should allow the script to identify the group.
verification_requirements: Verify that selecting 'No symptoms' via keyboard (Tab/Space) or mouse clears any previously selected symptom checkboxes.
Verify that selecting a symptom checkbox after 'No symptoms' clears the 'No symptoms' checkbox.
Confirm that form data reflects the correct values after each interaction.
Ensure the contact group's exclusive 'Do not contact me' checkbox continues to work as expected.
Check that no visual or functional regressions are introduced.
